briefings.title: Bill Gates calls AI ‘the most dangerous technology’ ever invented
briefings.tldr: Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates warns that AI is the most dangerous technology ever invented—surpassing the societal impact of personal computers and the internet—and asserts that self-governance by tech companies is entirely insufficient to prevent catastrophic misuse.

briefings.title: AI is not a new species, it's software: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang
briefings.tldr: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang argues that AI is manageable software rather than an uncontrolled new species, asserting that companies warning about existential risks should simply exercise self-restraint or shut down unsafe experiments rather than relying solely on government intervention.

briefings.title: FULL INTERVIEW: CNN's Anderson Cooper Presses NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang Over Pace Of AI Development
briefings.tldr: NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang told CNN's Anderson Cooper that AI safety is paramount and risks can be managed through engineering controls like sandboxing and continuous monitoring, dismissing apocalyptic fears of human extinction by 2030 as ungrounded.

briefings.title: The Future of War and Global Power: Can the West Innovate Fast Enough?

people.name: Dan Driscoll
people.role: Former United States Secretary of the Army

briefings.tldr: Eric Schmidt and Dan Driscoll discuss how software-driven warfare and rapid AI integration are transforming global conflict in Ukraine, arguing that Western defense ecosystems must urgently modernize their data infrastructure, adopt open architecture, and scale hardware production to outpace adversaries.

briefings.title: US and China: From Here to Where?
briefings.tldr: While deep structural forces continue to drive a fierce "Thucydidean" rivalry between the US and China, the bilateral summit has successfully established a temporary framework of "constructive strategic stability," allowing global businesses to navigate geopolitical volatility through highly localized strategies and targeted cooperation.
